description.narrative: The Local Economic Transformation Program (LET Program) is an initiative that strengthens district and municipal capacities to i) expand their own-source revenues (OSR), manage resources in a participatory and transparent way, and ii) drive local economic development through investments and partnerships with the private sector, and iii) co-design a sustainable financing facility for public investment projects and revenue-generating opportunities for youth- and women-led MSMEs.The Program builds on UNDP’s Integrated Local Finance Framework methodology and previous Localization of SDGs project, Decentralization for Development (D4D) and Initiatives to Promote Decentralization in Niassa and Nampula provinces (I4D) projects, implemented between 2021 and 2026 in Maputo, Manica, Sofala, Cabo Delgado, Niassa and Nampula provinces. These were focused on enhancing local participatory and data-driven planning, SDG localization, budgeting, digitalization of public finances and local services, as well as investing in key social and economic infrastructures and economic activities at district level.Aligned with the National Development Strategy, Territorial Development Strategies, the draft National Public Finance Strategy and contributing to the Government of Mozambique’s (GoM) National Local Economic Development Program, LET prioritizes actions that catalyze local revenue mobilization, value addition, strengthen market linkages, and promote transparent and inclusive public finance management and economic transformation. The Program is implemented in partnership with MPD, MF, MAEFP, CTA, the Association of Industrialization of Mozambique (AIMO), financial sector institutions, ANAMM and UEM.
